_readme: William's decisions from import-report.md. warband_aliases: a source warband name -> type slugs ([] leaves it out); MiM restrictions use them too; one that keeps the mapping the build would make reads as settled in the report. extra_warband_types: warbands neither Broheim nor mordheimer lists (its setting and source, and its grade and Broheim PDF where it has them). drop_warband_types: a Broheim warband left out -> why (one William split into two, whose types are extra_warband_types entries); the seeder archives the type it drops. warband_type_names: a type's name as Broheim spells it -> as we show it (a typo or a capital "Of"; the slug stays the source's). persona_item_names: a name a dramatis persona's kit prints -> our item it means, for one that is ours under another word (Heinrich 'Altdorf' Schmidt's Whip is our Steel Whip; the Khemri equipment page prints no whip of its own, 11 Nov 2026). persona_names: a dramatis persona's name as mordheimer gives it -> ours (one casing: title case, small words lower case after the first; William, 5 Nov 2026). group_members: add/remove type slugs per group slug, and keep_in/keep_out the types William keeps in or out of a group (held there); each settles its types' group questions. setting_grades: setting slug -> grade. keep_hidden_items: mordheimer items it hides that should be imported anyway. drop_items: mordheimer items left out. item_names: a mordheimer item's name -> the name we show it under (name), the tags added with it (tags), the tags dropped (drop_tags), the kind and subtype it takes (type, subtype: the Magic Carpet is an Animal, a Mount, since the bestiary holds it), the range, strength or save it takes where mordheimer's is wrong (the Nehekharan Javelins' 8", 12" in their warband's own PDF) and why. item_warbands: item name -> the only type slugs that may buy it, and why. item_warbands_add: item name -> type slugs added to its mordheimer list, and why. item_exclusions: item name -> the only type slugs an item for everyone shuts out, and why. item_defaults_kept: item name -> why the default its contradictions took stands. item_own_rules: our item's name -> the rules William settles for it (rules: name, summary, text), in place of its own. item_notes: item name -> a soft note added to each of its price rows. item_rule_wordings: a shared item rule's slug -> the wording William settles for it (summary, text), the items whose own wording it now covers (covers: their own is dropped) and those that keep only what is theirs (items: name -> summary, text). whole_names: names matched as a whole on the same-name list, not split at the slash. setting_assignments: kind (skills, hired_swords, dramatis_personae) -> our row's name as the report shows it ("Sniper (Hochland Bandits)") -> setting slug (one mordheimer gives several settings is then settled). skill_lists: a skill list's name -> who learns the skills of it mordheimer lacks (for_everyone, or warbands as {type} or {group} slugs), large_only (a Large unit's skill) and a note shown when learning. drop_skills: our skill rows left out (label -> why). extra_skills: skill rows our table lacks. skill_descriptions: a skill row's description put right (label -> text). fees_in_rules: a hired sword's or dramatis persona's name -> why its hire fee is in its rules: kind special, its gold kept, its hiring sentence in full as the note. hire_warbands_add: a hired sword's or dramatis persona's name -> type slugs added to its mordheimer hire list, and why (a list that then matches a group is stored as that group, so it follows the group). Skill groups (phase 1a): our skill rows merge by name into one skill each, linked into the group of every list that had it, and each list is a group; a list's skill_lists decision is its group's (who learns from it, large_only, note). skill_splits: a row (by label) whose rule differs stays its own skill under name, in its group alone, and why. skill_wordings: a merged skill's name -> the wording it takes (text, or the row label it is from) and why; any other merged skill keeps its longest. skill_group_learners: a group's name -> who learns from it (for_everyone, or warbands as {type} or {group} slugs), settling a group the report flags (its default is the warbands that may learn every skill in it). new_skill_groups: groups our lists lack -> the warband type that alone learns from it (type, or types), our skills it holds (skills) and new ones (new_skills; {name, rule} names one apart from the skill whose rules it takes) with rules from mordheimer, or from the source file in sources/ it names. seed_items_back: an item of our old seed (apps/items/data/standard-items.json) -> the setting and source it comes back with, and why: its price rows and properties as they were, single use kept. extra_items: items no source has: name, type, subtype, setting, source, cost, the warband types that buy it, the price row's note, and why. warband_items: an item a warband's special equipment brings in (warband_items.py) -> the snapshot page (testwarbands-2026-10-31), the entry when it is named otherwise, the warband type that buys it, its type and subtype: one price row for that type at the book's price and rarity.

rules.summary: Thrown; D3 S4 hits with no armour save, S3 within 1"
rules.text: A fire bomb is thrown in the shooting phase, with a range of twice the thrower's Strength in inches. Roll to hit with his Ballistic Skill, with no modifier for range or moving. A hit causes D3 Strength 4 hits with no armour save, and every warrior within 1", friend or foe, takes one Strength 3 hit with saves as normal. On a roll of 1 to hit, the bomb misfires and explodes as though it had hit the thrower.

Fire Bomb.why: The Innocents PDF (p8) prints the fire bomb's rules and ours had none

rules.summary: Thrown as an enemy charges; he strikes last unless he passes an Initiative test
rules.text: A smoke bomb may be thrown as an enemy charges the wielder, interrupting the charge. The charger is placed in base contact and must pass an Initiative test at once. If he fails he is blinded and strikes last in the hand-to-hand combat phase whatever his Initiative or his skills.

Smoke Bomb.why: The Innocents PDF (p8) prints the smoke bomb's rules and ours had none

rules.summary: Keeps the wearer's equipment dry; over armour, never with a cloak
rules.text: A rain coat keeps its wearer, and above all his equipment and his blackpowder, dry in wet weather. It may be worn over armour with no penalty, but never together with a cloak, and it is no help against the water a model walks or falls into. It is an exception to the normal rules, in that a Henchman may have one.

Rain Coat.why: William, 11 Nov 2026: the Sartosa Greatcoat is our Rain Coat ("Based on 'Raincoat' from Border Town Burning", 10 gc), and its two clauses - worn over armour but not with a cloak, and no help in water terrain - fold into ours, which said only that a Henchman may have one and left what it does to its flavour line

rules.summary: Flying mount with 16" movement; destroyed outright by fire
rules.text: A magic carpet is indeed just that – a carpet that flies! It counts as a mount and allows movement of 16" with no restrictions for terrain. You can move onto the roofs of buildings and other high places with no penalty. The carpet may carry up to three men or one large creature and a man. One of the riders must be a character. Due to its magical nature it cannot be destroyed, except by fire: taken out of action by fire it is destroyed outright, with no roll on the Henchmen injury chart.

Magic Carpet.why: William, 12 Nov 2026: the Khemri equipment page destroys the carpet by fire where ours said only that its magical nature means it cannot be destroyed, so the fire rule is added to ours; the bestiary mount already carried it

rules.summary: Strength test to acquire; +1 armour save against shooting
rules.text: To acquire the cloak a warrior must pay 10 gc, for the travel and the hunt, and roll equal to or under his Strength on a D6. If he succeeds he finds and slays the beast and wears its cloak. A warband whose own equipment list sells the cloak may buy one when the warband is raised without testing for availability. A model wearing it gains +1 to his armour saves against all shooting attacks.

Wolfcloak.why: William, 12 Nov 2026: the Mazzalupo's Bearcloak is our Wolfcloak, "reworded away from the wolf". Ours named the wolf, the Hero and Middenheim, where the Mazzalupo's names a bear and a Sheepherder; the numbers, the Strength test and the +1 save against shooting are the same in both, so one wording serves them both

two-handed.summary: Needs both hands; no shield, buckler or second weapon in close combat
two-handed.text: A model armed with this weapon needs both hands for it, so he may not use a shield, buckler or additional weapon in close combat. If he carries a shield he still gets its +1 armour save bonus against shooting.
two-handed.why: William, 11 Nov 2026: "people always get the +1 save from having a shield for 2 handed weapons, its not specific to either and really should be mentioned within the 2-handed rule for every weapon that uses that rule"

Serpent Staff.text: The Serpent Staff may be used to parry.

parry.why: the Serpent Staff worded its two rules as one sentence, the half left by the Two-handed rule's own wording

skill_descriptions.Quick Thinker (Dwarf Exiled Engineers): The dwarf may add +1 to any roll on the experimental weapons chart. (MiM)
skill_descriptions.Trap Expert (Academic): This Hero is able to detect traps in the tombs with relative ease. A character who possesses this skill will never set off traps himself (but may be subject to their effects if he is too close when it goes off). He can attempt to disarm traps by stopping at the trap during his Movement phase, and may do nothing else that turn. To disarm a Simple trap, roll 6+ on 2D6. To disarm a Complex trap, roll 8+ on 2D6. If unsuccessful, he must test against his Initiative; a failed test means he sets off the trap himself. He can also attempt to restore dud or previously de-activated traps: roll a D6 (1-4 Simple, 5-6 Complex), then roll 6+ on 2D6 to restore a Simple trap or 8+ on 2D6 for a Complex trap. Failure means the trap fails to activate. Either half may be taken up to four times, taking 1 off its roll each time, so that at the limit a Simple trap is disarmed on a 2+ and a Complex trap on a 4+.

rules.name: Pox
rules.summary: A 6 to hit takes 1 Toughness for that combat phase
rules.text: On a roll of 6 to hit, the model hit loses 1 Toughness for the rest of that combat phase. Undead, possessed and daemonic models are not affected.
